accuracy.evidence: The routine and its origin are checked against Lyman (1981), who set out think-pair-share to include every student in class discussion. The wait-time claim (3 seconds or more after a question gives more children answering and longer answers) is Rowe (1986). The Key Stage 1 link is the National Curriculum (2014) spoken language statements (listen and respond appropriately, articulate and justify answers, take turns in discussions). The EEF Teaching and Learning Toolkit rates oral language approaches as high impact for very low cost. The class of 12 in the timer scene is labelled as made up in the scene text and the adult text, so no invented statistic is presented as data. Big snowmen melting more slowly is correct (less surface for their volume).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in the adult text: answering at once so only the fastest think (timer at 0-1 s shows 2 of 12, predict 1, 'fast', m1), shouting out ('shout' card refused, challenge), copying a partner ('Wait and copy Mia' refused, 'copy'), keeping the turn (saying your idea twice refused, 'hog', m3), not listening ('I was not listening' and 'think about my next idea' refused, predict 3, 'listen', p3), saying your own idea back as hers ('mine', m4), sharing only your idea or 'I think' ('onlymine', 'me', predict 4, m9), no reason ('noreason', m6), unkind words about a partner's idea ('unkind') and the wrong order ('order', 'nothink', m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtps models the routine itself: a draggable think timer over a made-up class where each child lights a bulb at their own ready time, a think bubble with idea and because slots, a talk-turn token that must be passed to Mia before she speaks followed by a say-it-back check, a three-row We think / idea / because sentence builder that refuses one-sided or reasonless shares, and a 1-2-3 ordering of the steps. 217 Building on others (flagbuildon) adds to an idea, 163 Exploring ideas through talk (flagwonder) generates maybes, and 495 Thinking aloud (flagtloud) narrates a task; none has wait time, turn passing or a pair share. Shingle similarity is under 30% against every flag_*.js (gate passes).

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the reason for each step by doing it: dragging the timer from 0 to 5 seconds lifts the ideas count from 0 to 2, 7 and then 10 of 12, so the value of quiet think time is seen, not told; the think bubble only accepts your own idea and a because reason; the turn token cannot pass before you speak and you cannot speak twice; the say-back check needs Mia's words, not yours; the share button names the first weak row (I think, my idea only, no reason). Done messages confirm after the action.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Everyone did' get to think when the first hand is picked (the timer at 1 s shows only 2 of 12 ready), 'Think about my next idea' while Mia talks (the say-back check then needs her idea, and the planning option is refused as not listening), and 'Just mine' to share (the 'build it in the shade' only card is refused for leaving out Mia's idea).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions whose wrong answers carry ten distinct slip messages: shout, copy, hog, listen, mine, unkind, me, noidea, noreason, order and time (some children need more seconds to have an idea). Each names the specific slip and what to do instead; checked on phone screenshots, a wrong first answer shows 'Shouting out takes away everyone else's think time. Think quietly first.'

readability.evidence: Kid text is four short paragraphs in plain words (think, pair, share, turn, listen, because) and passes the learner readability limit in validate_lessons.py; lab cards are two to ten words. Adult text passes its limit while keeping the precise terms (wait time, spoken language, justify, structured talk) and naming the researchers.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one step or the reason for think time; the adult paragraphs give the origin and curriculum link, the job of each step with the wait-time research, the named mistakes with a caution about cutting think time, and what the lab does. No content-gate filler matches; lab text is the question, the cards and feedback.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android screenshots in light and dark, before and after Show me, for every step: the 4 by 3 class grid with bulbs, the ideas count and the 0-10 s timer with a 16 px knob fit with room to drag; the think bubble's two slots sit above a 2 by 2 card grid; Me and Mia cards sit side by side with wrapped speech; the 3 by 3 share grid wraps long cards to four lines without clipping and options are rotated so the right card is not always first; the 1-2-3 boxes fit across. walk.cjs passed on iPhone 13 and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Wait 1 more second and Ask now for the timer, one button per think card, Say my idea and Pass the turn to Mia, one button per say-back answer, one per share card plus Share with the class, and Pick then Put in box 1-3 for ordering; cards can also be tapped then the target tapped. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each scene description and feedback, challenge feedback is a role=status live region, chosen and wrong cards carry ✓ / ✗ / ● text as well as colour, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in light and dark on desktop and phone.
